fields.title: All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
fields.author: Larry Wasserman

fields.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python
fields.author: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jonathan Taylor

fields.title: Analysis of Financial Time Series, 3rd Edition
fields.author: Ruey S. Tsay

fields.title: A Practical Guide to Quantitative Finance Interviews
fields.author: Xinfeng Zhou

fields.name: Probability with Blitzstein & Hwang
fields.description: Chapters 1-11 of Introduction to Probability, one chapter per week, with Harvard Stat 110 lectures and problem sets. Builds the probability foundation that every later roadmap assumes, up to and including Markov chains.

fields.name: Statistical Inference with Wasserman
fields.description: Chapters 5-13 of All of Statistics, one chapter (or half-chapter) per week: convergence, estimation, bootstrap, maximum likelihood, testing, multiple testing, Bayesian inference, decision theory and regression. The theory that quant research and interviews assume.

fields.name: Machine Learning with ISLP
fields.description: Chapters 2-6, 8, 10, 12 and 13 of An Introduction to Statistical Learning (Python edition), one chapter per week with its lab, ending in a return-prediction project with walk-forward validation.

fields.name: Financial Time Series with Tsay
fields.description: Chapters 1, 2, 3, 8, 9 and 11 of Analysis of Financial Time Series, one chapter (or half-chapter) per week, with Hyndman's free Forecasting: Principles and Practice as a gentler reference. Stationarity, ARMA, GARCH, cointegration, factor models and the Kalman filter.

fields.name: Financial Machine Learning with López de Prado
fields.description: Chapters 2-12 and 14-17 of Advances in Financial Machine Learning, one or two chapters per week: data structures, labeling, sample weights, fractional differentiation, purged cross-validation, feature importance, bet sizing, backtest statistics and HRP. Read the time series roadmap first.

fields.name: Interview Readiness for ML Quant Roles
fields.description: The six things beyond the core books, one week each: linear algebra (two weeks), timed quant problem practice (two weeks), coding interviews, ML interview depth, finance vocabulary and a capstone project you can defend (two weeks).

fields.name: Probability and Counting
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 1. Sample spaces, the naive definition of probability, counting rules and the axioms.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 1 problem set with written solutions to at least 20 exercises.

fields.name: Conditional Probability
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 2. Conditioning, Bayes' rule, independence and conditioning as a problem-solving tool.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 2 problem set; a half-page explanation of Bayes' rule with a worked base-rate example.

fields.name: Random Variables and Their Distributions
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 3. Random variables as functions, PMFs, CDFs and the first named discrete distributions.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 3 problem set; a one-page cheat sheet of named discrete distributions with their stories.

fields.name: Expectation
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 4. Expectation, linearity, indicator random variables, variance and the Poisson distribution.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 4 problem set, including the coupon-collector problem solved with indicators.

fields.name: Continuous Random Variables
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 5. Densities, the uniform, normal and exponential distributions, and the Poisson process.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 5 problem set; a short script generating normal and exponential samples from uniforms.

fields.name: Moments
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 6. Moments, skewness, kurtosis, moment generating functions and heavy-tailed returns.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 6 problem set; a notebook computing sample moments of real return series against a normal fit.

fields.name: Joint Distributions
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 7. Joint, marginal and conditional distributions, covariance, correlation and the multivariate normal.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 7 problem set; a one-page summary of covariance rules and the multivariate normal.

fields.name: Transformations
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 8. Change of variables, convolutions, Beta and Gamma distributions, and order statistics.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 8 problem set; a derivation of the distribution of the maximum of n uniforms.

fields.name: Conditional Expectation
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 9. Conditional expectation given an event or a random variable, Adam's and Eve's laws, and prediction.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 9 problem set; a worked example of Eve's law on a compound-sum problem.

fields.name: Inequalities and Limit Theorems
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 10. Markov, Chebyshev, Jensen and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities; the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 10 problem set; a notebook that simulates the CLT from three different distributions.

fields.name: Markov Chains
fields.description: Blitzstein & Hwang ch. 11. The Markov property, transition matrices, stationary distributions and reversibility.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 11 problem set; a notebook that computes and simulates a stationary distribution.

fields.name: Probability Review and Consolidation
fields.description: Mixed review across all chapters plus a small simulation project to confirm the material is usable, not just read.
fields.deliverable: 30 mixed review problems, the Monte Carlo mini-project notebook, and a self-assessment with weak areas listed.

fields.name: Convergence of Random Variables
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 5. Modes of convergence, the law of large numbers and CLT with proofs, and the delta method.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 5 exercises; a derivation of the asymptotic variance of the Sharpe ratio by the delta method.

fields.name: Models, Statistical Inference and Learning
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 6. Parametric and nonparametric models, point estimation, confidence sets and the vocabulary of inference.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 6 exercises; a one-page summary of estimator properties (bias, SE, MSE, consistency).

fields.name: Estimating the CDF and Statistical Functionals
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 7. The empirical distribution function, plug-in estimators and statistical functionals.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 7 exercises; a plot of an empirical CDF with its DKW confidence band.

fields.name: The Bootstrap
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 8. Bootstrap variance estimation and confidence intervals, with a finance application.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 8 exercises; a notebook bootstrapping the Sharpe ratio with ordinary and block bootstrap.

fields.name: Method of Moments and Maximum Likelihood
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 9, first half. Method of moments and the properties of maximum likelihood estimators.
fields.deliverable: Written MLE derivations and asymptotic variances for at least five distributions.

fields.name: Fisher Information and the Cramér-Rao Bound
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 9, second half. Fisher information, efficiency, multiparameter models and the parametric bootstrap.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 9 exercises; a notebook comparing information-based and bootstrap standard errors for a Student-t fit.

fields.name: Hypothesis Testing and p-values
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 10, first half. The Neyman-Pearson framework, Wald, likelihood ratio and chi-square tests, and p-values.
fields.deliverable: Test-construction exercises; a half-page on what a p-value is and is not.

fields.name: Multiple Testing
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 10, second half. Family-wise error rate, false discovery rate, and why this is the central statistical problem in strategy research.
fields.deliverable: A notebook running hundreds of tests on random signals with Bonferroni and BH corrections, plus a written FWER-versus-FDR explanation.

fields.name: Bayesian Inference
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 11. Priors, posteriors, conjugacy, Bayesian intervals and the Bayesian view of regularization.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 11 exercises; a worked Normal-Normal update and a note on how priors give ridge and lasso.

fields.name: Statistical Decision Theory
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 12. Loss and risk, Bayes and minimax estimators, admissibility and James-Stein shrinkage.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 12 exercises; a short simulation showing James-Stein beating the sample mean.

fields.name: Linear and Logistic Regression
fields.description: Wasserman ch. 13. Least squares in matrix form, inference for coefficients, model selection and logistic regression.
fields.deliverable: Chapter 13 exercises; a derivation of the OLS estimator and its covariance in matrix form.

fields.name: Regression Diagnostics and Hypothesis-Testing Project
fields.description: Apply the inference toolkit: regression diagnostics on real returns and a small project that tests a trading hypothesis properly.
fields.deliverable: The regression-diagnostics notebook; the multiple-testing mini-project write-up; self-assessment with weak areas listed.

fields.name: Statistical Learning
fields.description: ISLP ch. 2. What statistical learning is, the bias-variance trade-off and how to assess model accuracy.
fields.deliverable: Lab 2 completed; environment ready for all later labs; a written bias-variance explanation.

fields.name: Linear Regression
fields.description: ISLP ch. 3. Simple and multiple linear regression, interactions, qualitative predictors and diagnostics.
fields.deliverable: Lab 3 completed; chapter 3 exercises.

fields.name: Classification
fields.description: ISLP ch. 4. Logistic regression, discriminant analysis, naive Bayes, KNN and generalized linear models.
fields.deliverable: Lab 4 completed; a comparison table of logistic regression, LDA, QDA and KNN on the Smarket data.

fields.name: Resampling Methods
fields.description: ISLP ch. 5. Cross-validation and the bootstrap, and why standard cross-validation breaks on time series.
fields.deliverable: Lab 5 completed; a working walk-forward cross-validation splitter in Python.

fields.name: Linear Model Selection and Regularization
fields.description: ISLP ch. 6. Subset selection, ridge, lasso, dimension reduction and high-dimensional data.
fields.deliverable: Lab 6 completed; a notebook with ridge and lasso paths and CV-chosen penalties.

fields.name: Tree-Based Methods
fields.description: ISLP ch. 8. Decision trees, bagging, random forests, boosting and BART.
fields.deliverable: Lab 8 completed; a notebook comparing random forest and boosting with feature importances.

fields.name: Deep Learning
fields.description: ISLP ch. 10. Neural networks, convolutional and recurrent architectures, and how networks are fitted.
fields.deliverable: Lab 10 completed; a small PyTorch model trained on a return-prediction task.

fields.name: Unsupervised Learning
fields.description: ISLP ch. 12. Principal components, clustering and matrix completion.
fields.deliverable: Lab 12 completed; PCA and clustering notebook on a panel of stock returns.

fields.name: Multiple Testing
fields.description: ISLP ch. 13. Family-wise error rate, false discovery rate and resampling approaches, applied to strategy selection.
fields.deliverable: Lab 13 completed; a notebook showing how many random signals survive Bonferroni and BH.

fields.name: ISLP Project: Return Prediction with Walk-Forward Validation
fields.description: Apply the ISLP toolkit to real market data with honest validation.
fields.deliverable: Project notebook comparing four models under walk-forward validation, with a write-up of out-of-sample results.

fields.name: Financial Time Series and Their Characteristics
fields.description: Tsay ch. 1. Asset returns, their distributional properties and the stylized facts of financial data.
fields.deliverable: Exploration notebook on return distributions and autocorrelations at several horizons.

fields.name: Stationarity and ARMA Models
fields.description: Tsay ch. 2, first half (Hyndman ch. 2, 5 and 9 as a gentler alternative). Stationarity, autocorrelation and ARMA modeling.
fields.deliverable: ARMA fits with Ljung-Box diagnostics on at least three return series.

fields.name: Unit Roots and Regression with Time Series
fields.description: Tsay ch. 2, second half. Random walks, unit-root tests, spurious regression and seasonality.
fields.deliverable: ADF-test notebook plus the spurious-regression simulation with a short written interpretation.

fields.name: Conditional Heteroscedastic Models
fields.description: Tsay ch. 3. ARCH and GARCH models for volatility clustering, asymmetric extensions and volatility forecasting.
fields.deliverable: GARCH notebook with symmetric and asymmetric fits and forecast evaluation against realized volatility.

fields.name: Multivariate Time Series and Cointegration
fields.description: Tsay ch. 8. Vector autoregression, cointegration tests, error-correction models and pairs trading.
fields.deliverable: Pairs-trading backtest sketch on a cointegrated pair, with transaction costs included.

fields.name: Principal Component Analysis and Factor Models
fields.description: Tsay ch. 9. PCA of return panels, statistical factor models and factor regressions.
fields.deliverable: PCA notebook on a stock universe with loadings, scree plot and a market-beta comparison.

fields.name: State-Space Models and the Kalman Filter
fields.description: Tsay ch. 11. State-space representation, the Kalman filter and smoother, and time-varying parameter models.
fields.deliverable: Kalman-filter notebook with a local-level model and a time-varying beta example.

fields.name: Financial Data Structures
fields.description: AFML ch. 1-2. Why standard ML fails in finance and how to build information-driven bars.
fields.deliverable: Notebook building dollar bars from intraday data and comparing them with time bars.

fields.name: Labeling
fields.description: AFML ch. 3. Fixed-horizon labels, the triple-barrier method and meta-labeling.
fields.deliverable: Notebook implementing triple-barrier labels with a check of label balance and duration.

fields.name: Sample Weights
fields.description: AFML ch. 4. Overlapping outcomes, label uniqueness, sequential bootstrap and time-decay weights.
fields.deliverable: Uniqueness-based sample weights added to the labels.

fields.name: Fractionally Differentiated Features
fields.description: AFML ch. 5. The stationarity-memory trade-off and fractional differentiation.
fields.deliverable: Fractional-differentiation notebook with the minimum d found.

fields.name: Ensemble Methods and Cross-Validation in Finance
fields.description: AFML ch. 6-7. Ensembles under non-IID data, leakage, and purged k-fold with embargo.
fields.deliverable: A PurgedKFold implementation with a comparison against plain k-fold on the labeled data.

fields.name: Feature Importance and Hyper-Parameter Tuning
fields.description: AFML ch. 8-9. MDI, MDA and single-feature importance, orthogonal features, and tuning with purged CV.
fields.deliverable: MDI/MDA/SFI importance comparison on the model.

fields.name: Bet Sizing
fields.description: AFML ch. 10. Turning predicted probabilities into position sizes.
fields.deliverable: A bet-sizing function from predicted probabilities.

fields.name: Backtesting and Its Dangers
fields.description: AFML ch. 11, 12 and 14. Backtesting errors, combinatorial purged CV and backtest statistics.
fields.deliverable: Deflated Sharpe ratio notebook on a family of strategies; one-page summary of backtesting pitfalls.

fields.name: Strategy Risk and Machine Learning Asset Allocation
fields.description: AFML ch. 15-16. The probability a strategy fails, and hierarchical risk parity.
fields.deliverable: HRP portfolio notebook with an out-of-sample variance comparison.

fields.name: Structural Breaks and Feature Engineering
fields.description: AFML ch. 17-19. Break tests, entropy features and microstructural features, in overview.
fields.deliverable: CUSUM test applied to one series.

fields.name: Capstone: End-to-End Financial ML Pipeline
fields.description: Assemble the techniques into one reproducible pipeline and evaluate it honestly.
fields.deliverable: End-to-end pipeline repository with combinatorial-CV results, DSR and a write-up.

fields.name: Linear Algebra I: Systems, Subspaces and Projections
fields.description: MIT 18.06 lectures 1-17 with Strang. Elimination, vector spaces and least squares as projection.
fields.deliverable: 18.06 problem sets for lectures 1-17; a derivation of the normal equations from projection.

fields.name: Linear Algebra II: Eigenvalues, SVD and Covariance
fields.description: MIT 18.06 lectures 18-31 with Strang. Eigen-decomposition, positive-definite matrices and the SVD, applied to covariance and PCA.
fields.deliverable: 18.06 problem sets for lectures 18-31; NumPy implementations of PCA and least squares verified against libraries.

fields.name: Brainteasers and Probability Problems
fields.description: Zhou's green book, chapters 2-4: timed practice on brainteasers and probability questions.
fields.deliverable: At least 80 solved problems from the green book with a log of error patterns.

fields.name: Statistics, Stochastic Processes and Mock Interviews
fields.description: Zhou's green book, chapters 5-6, plus recorded mock interviews.
fields.deliverable: At least 70 more solved problems; two recorded mock interviews reviewed.

fields.name: Algorithms Refresher
fields.description: Medium-difficulty algorithm problems on the patterns quant coding rounds use most.
fields.deliverable: 60 medium LeetCode problems with complexity analysis noted for each.

fields.name: NumPy and pandas for Live Data Tasks
fields.description: The data-manipulation fluency tested in live coding sessions.
fields.deliverable: Three timed pandas data tasks completed.

fields.name: Machine Learning Interview Depth
fields.description: Be able to explain core ML ideas from scratch, out loud, to both ML and non-ML interviewers.
fields.deliverable: Written two-minute explanations of five ML concepts, rehearsed aloud.

fields.name: Finance Vocabulary and Market Basics
fields.description: Enough market knowledge to follow a trading-floor conversation and frame a model's purpose.
fields.deliverable: A one-page finance glossary.

fields.name: Capstone: Design and Build
fields.description: One honest project on real market data: fix the protocol first, then build and validate.
fields.deliverable: Protocol document written before modeling; working backtest with out-of-sample, cost-adjusted results.

fields.name: Capstone: Write-up, Walkthrough and Final Mock Loop
fields.description: Make the project reproducible and defensible, then rehearse the whole interview loop.
fields.deliverable: Capstone repository with README and report; rehearsed walkthrough; one full mock interview loop completed.

fields.topic_name: Sample spaces and the naive definition of probability
fields.description: Define experiments, sample spaces and events; compute probabilities by counting equally likely outcomes.

fields.topic_name: Counting: multiplication rule, permutations and binomial coefficients
fields.description: The counting tools behind most discrete probability problems, including sampling with and without replacement.

fields.topic_name: Story proofs and the axioms of probability
fields.description: Prove combinatorial identities by interpretation; learn the axioms and inclusion-exclusion.
Work at least 20 exercises, including the birthday problem and de Montmort's matching problem.
Definition of conditioning, Bayes' rule, prior and posterior odds, the base-rate fallacy.

fields.topic_name: Law of total probability and independence
fields.description: Partition the sample space to compute probabilities; independence versus conditional independence; Simpson's paradox.

fields.topic_name: Conditioning as a tool: first-step analysis and gambler's ruin
fields.description: Solve recursive problems by conditioning on the first step; the gambler's ruin problem and its finance interpretation.
Exercises on Bayes' rule, the Monty Hall problem and conditional independence.
Random variables as maps from the sample space; probability mass functions and cumulative distribution functions.

fields.topic_name: Bernoulli, binomial, hypergeometric and discrete uniform
fields.description: Stories behind the core discrete distributions and when each applies.

fields.topic_name: Functions of random variables and independence
fields.description: Distributions of transformed random variables; independence and i.i.d. samples.
Exercises on identifying distributions from stories and computing PMFs.
Definition of expected value and the power of linearity for sums of dependent random variables.

fields.topic_name: Geometric, negative binomial and indicator random variables
fields.description: Waiting-time distributions and the indicator trick for counting problems.

fields.topic_name: LOTUS, variance and the Poisson distribution
fields.description: Law of the unconscious statistician, variance and standard deviation, Poisson as a limit of binomials.
Exercises using indicators and linearity, including the coupon collector and St. Petersburg problems.

fields.topic_name: PDFs, CDFs and the uniform distribution
fields.description: Probability density functions, universality of the uniform and how to generate random variables from it.
Standard normal, location-scale transformations, the 68-95-99.7 rule and why normality appears everywhere.

fields.topic_name: Exponential distribution and the Poisson process
fields.description: Memorylessness, rates, and inter-arrival times; first look at the Poisson process.
Exercises on densities, transformations and memorylessness.
Higher moments, what skewness and kurtosis measure, and why financial returns are fat-tailed.
MGFs, sums of independent random variables and the MGF of the normal distribution.

fields.topic_name: Python: sample moments of real return series
fields.description: Download daily prices, compute returns, and estimate skewness and kurtosis with SciPy; compare with a normal fit.
Exercises on moments and MGFs.
Two-dimensional PMFs and PDFs, marginalization and conditioning in the discrete and continuous cases.
Definitions, properties, variance of sums, and correlation as a measure of linear dependence only.
Covariance matrices, linear combinations of jointly normal variables and the multivariate normal density.
Exercises on joint densities, covariance and the bivariate normal.
The Jacobian method for transformations and the distribution of sums of independent random variables.
Stories and conjugacy relationships; Beta-Binomial and Gamma-Poisson.
Distributions of the minimum, maximum and j-th order statistic.
Exercises on transformations and order statistics.

fields.topic_name: Conditional expectation given an event and given a random variable
fields.description: Conditional expectation as a random variable; taking out what is known.
Law of total expectation and law of total variance, with applications to mixtures and compound sums.
Conditional expectation as the best predictor in mean squared error; the link to regression.
Exercises on Adam's and Eve's laws and prediction problems.
The core inequalities and how they bound tail probabilities and expectations.

fields.topic_name: Law of large numbers and central limit theorem
fields.description: Statements, intuition and sketch proofs; what the CLT does and does not say about heavy tails.

fields.topic_name: Python: simulate the CLT and chi-square and t distributions
fields.description: Simulate sample means from several distributions, check convergence to normal, and see where the t distribution comes from.
Exercises on inequalities and limit theorems.
Define Markov chains, n-step transition probabilities and matrix powers.

fields.topic_name: Classification of states and stationary distributions
fields.description: Recurrent and transient states, irreducibility, periodicity, existence and uniqueness of the stationary distribution.

fields.topic_name: Reversibility and random walks on graphs
fields.description: Detailed balance, reversible chains and random walks, with a preview of MCMC.
Exercises on stationary distributions and absorbing chains.
Solve 30 problems chosen across chapters 1-11 without looking up which chapter they came from.
Pick three results (e.g. gambler's ruin, coupon collector, a Markov chain stationary distribution) and verify them by Monte Carlo.
Attempt a timed set of 10 interview-style probability questions and record which topics need revisiting.
Convergence in probability, in distribution and in quadratic mean, and the relationships between them.

fields.topic_name: Law of large numbers and CLT revisited
fields.description: Proofs via Chebyshev and characteristic functions; the Berry-Esseen bound on CLT accuracy.
Asymptotic distributions of smooth functions of estimators; application to the Sharpe ratio.
Selected exercises on convergence and the delta method.
What a statistical model is, identifiability, and the trade-off between assumptions and flexibility.

fields.topic_name: Point estimation: bias, standard error, MSE and consistency
fields.description: The properties used to judge an estimator and the bias-variance decomposition of mean squared error.

fields.topic_name: Confidence sets and hypothesis testing overview
fields.description: The meaning of a confidence interval and of a test, before the detailed treatment in later chapters.
Exercises on bias and MSE of simple estimators.

fields.topic_name: Empirical distribution function and the DKW inequality
fields.description: Properties of the empirical CDF, Glivenko-Cantelli and a confidence band from the DKW inequality.
Estimate means, quantiles, correlations and other functionals by plugging in the empirical CDF.
Standard errors for plug-in estimators via the influence function; robustness intuition.
Exercises on the empirical CDF and plug-in estimation.
The resampling idea, simulation versus bootstrap, and when the bootstrap fails.
Normal, pivotal and percentile intervals and how they compare.

fields.topic_name: Python: bootstrap the Sharpe ratio of a return series
fields.description: Compute a Sharpe ratio, bootstrap its distribution, and compare the interval with the delta-method answer; try a block bootstrap.
Exercises on bootstrap intervals.
Match sample and population moments; consistency and asymptotic normality.

fields.topic_name: Maximum likelihood: consistency, equivariance and asymptotic normality
fields.description: Derive MLEs, understand why they are consistent and asymptotically normal, and compute their standard errors.
Derive MLEs for the Bernoulli, Poisson, exponential, normal and uniform models and check them numerically.

fields.topic_name: Fisher information and the Cramér-Rao bound
fields.description: Information as curvature of the log-likelihood; the lower bound on estimator variance and efficiency.

fields.topic_name: Multiparameter models and the parametric bootstrap
fields.description: Fisher information matrices, the multiparameter delta method and bootstrapping under a parametric model.

fields.topic_name: Python: MLE standard errors from Fisher information versus bootstrap
fields.description: Fit a Student-t to returns by maximum likelihood with SciPy and compare information-based and bootstrap standard errors.

fields.topic_name: Chapter 9 exercises on information and efficiency
fields.description: Exercises on Fisher information and the Cramér-Rao bound.

fields.topic_name: Neyman-Pearson framework, power and error types
fields.description: Null and alternative, Type I and II errors, size and power, and how to design a test.

fields.topic_name: Wald, likelihood ratio and chi-square tests
fields.description: Construct and interpret the standard large-sample tests; goodness of fit.

fields.topic_name: p-values: what they mean and do not mean
fields.description: Definition, distribution under the null, and common misinterpretations.
Exercises on building tests, computing power and interpreting p-values.

fields.topic_name: Family-wise error rate: Bonferroni and Holm
fields.description: How many tests inflate false positives and the corrections that control the family-wise error rate.
FDR versus FWER, the BH procedure, and when controlling FDR is the right choice.

fields.topic_name: Python: run many tests on random signals
fields.description: Test hundreds of random 'signals' against returns, then apply Bonferroni and BH and count what survives.
Exercises on FWER and FDR control.
Bayes' theorem for parameters; Beta-Binomial and Normal-Normal conjugate updates.

fields.topic_name: Bayesian point and interval estimation; large-sample behavior
fields.description: Posterior mean and MAP estimates, credible intervals and the Bernstein-von Mises connection to MLE.

fields.topic_name: Shrinkage and the Bayesian view of regularization
fields.description: How Gaussian and Laplace priors give ridge and lasso; shrinkage estimators for noisy means and covariances.
Exercises on conjugate updating and posterior intervals.

fields.topic_name: Loss, risk, Bayes and minimax estimators
fields.description: Compare estimators by their risk functions; Bayes risk and minimax criteria.
Why the sample mean is inadmissible in three or more dimensions, and what that implies for estimating many expected returns.
Exercises on risk functions and shrinkage.

fields.topic_name: Simple and multiple regression in matrix form
fields.description: Least squares as projection, the hat matrix, Gauss-Markov and the sampling distribution of coefficients.

fields.topic_name: Inference for coefficients and model selection
fields.description: Standard errors, t-tests, confidence intervals, Mallows' Cp, AIC, BIC and cross-validation.
The logistic model, maximum likelihood fitting and interpretation of coefficients.
Exercises on least squares derivations and regression inference.
Fit a factor regression on stock returns, check residuals, heteroscedasticity and collinearity, and use robust standard errors.

fields.topic_name: Mini-project: test a calendar or momentum effect with multiple-testing correction
fields.description: Test several candidate effects on historical returns, report raw and FDR-adjusted p-values, and bootstrap the effect sizes.
Solve 15 problems across chapters 5-13, then a timed set of 10 interview-style statistics questions; list weak areas.

fields.topic_name: Prediction versus inference; parametric and nonparametric methods
fields.description: Why we estimate f, the accuracy-interpretability trade-off and supervised versus unsupervised learning.

fields.topic_name: Bias-variance trade-off and assessing model accuracy
fields.description: Training versus test error, the bias-variance decomposition, and the Bayes classifier.

fields.topic_name: Lab: Python, NumPy, pandas and the ISLP package
fields.description: Work through the chapter 2 lab to set up the environment used by every later lab.
Estimating coefficients, assessing accuracy and the F-test for overall fit.

fields.topic_name: Interactions, qualitative predictors and potential problems
fields.description: Dummy variables, interaction terms, non-linearity, correlated errors, heteroscedasticity, outliers and collinearity.
Fit, diagnose and extend regression models using statsmodels and the ISLP helpers.
Conceptual and applied exercises on regression.
Odds, the logistic model, multinomial extension and interpretation.

fields.topic_name: LDA, QDA, naive Bayes and KNN
fields.description: Generative classifiers versus discriminative ones and when each wins; ROC curves and confusion matrices.
Poisson regression and the GLM family.
Fit classifiers on the Smarket data and compare them with proper held-out evaluation.

fields.topic_name: Cross-validation: validation set, LOOCV and k-fold
fields.description: Estimating test error, the bias-variance trade-off of k, and cross-validation for classification.
Resampling to estimate the variability of any estimator.

fields.topic_name: Why random k-fold fails on financial time series
fields.description: Leakage through autocorrelation and overlapping labels; preview of walk-forward and purged cross-validation.
Implement CV and bootstrap with scikit-learn, then write a simple walk-forward splitter.
Best subset, forward and backward stepwise selection; Cp, AIC, BIC, adjusted R-squared.
Shrinkage penalties, the geometry of L1 versus L2, selecting the tuning parameter by CV, and the Bayesian interpretation.
Dimension reduction methods and what goes wrong when p is comparable to n.
Fit ridge and lasso paths with scikit-learn and choose penalties with cross-validation.
Recursive binary splitting, pruning, and trees versus linear models.
Variance reduction by averaging, out-of-bag error and variable importance.
Sequential fitting to residuals, learning rate and depth, and the gradient boosting view used by XGBoost and LightGBM.

fields.topic_name: Lab: random forests and boosting in Python
fields.description: Fit forests and boosted models, tune them with CV and compare feature importances.
Hidden units, activations and why depth helps.

fields.topic_name: CNNs and RNNs; sequence models for time series
fields.description: Convolutional layers, recurrent networks and their use on sequential financial data.

fields.topic_name: Fitting neural networks: SGD, backpropagation, regularization and dropout
fields.description: How training works, the double-descent phenomenon and interpolation.
Work through the chapter 10 lab, then fit a small network on a return-prediction task.
PCA as variance maximization and as low-rank approximation; proportion of variance explained.
Clustering algorithms, choosing the number of clusters and the pitfalls of clustering.
Low-rank imputation and its use on incomplete data.

fields.topic_name: Lab: PCA and clustering in Python
fields.description: Run PCA on a panel of stock returns and cluster assets by return correlation.
Why many tests inflate false positives; Bonferroni and Holm corrections.
Controlling FDR instead of FWER and when that is the right choice.
